decision: scoped this run to build phases 1-3 with a fake AI client
why: operator picked phases 1-3 first and has no API key for tests

decision: done = pytest green plus scripts/e2e.py driving the real CLI and server through login, capture and the checklist gate
why: check the real product, not just unit tests

decision: built auth as plain functions over the DB with an injectable clock: argon2, sessions, CSRF, lockout, TOTP, device flow, rotating refresh
why: lets tests drive lockout, expiry and device polling without sleeping

decision: fixed TOTP check to use the injected clock instead of wall time
recomputed the htmx SRI hash from the CDN file instead of trusting the one written from memory
why: never ship an integrity hash nobody checked

decision: added projects.checklist_built_at and regenerated the initial migration
why: auto-start on check needed an explicit built marker, not a guess from requirements version

decision: lowered priority bands to high>=4, medium>=2.5
why: a high-severity 40-minute failure scored medium, against requirements 9.3

decision: approved rules apply to every project and replace failure items in their category
why: requirements do not define rule matching; global keeps v1 simple and avoids duplicate items

decision: search now covers the first-guess field too
why: e2e search for a word only in the guess found nothing

decision: simulated offline by stopping the server on the same URL instead of pointing at a dead port
why: a different URL also meant different stored credentials, so the check measured the wrong thing

decision: broke offline replay idempotency on purpose to prove the checks can fail
why: 49 checks passing could mean the harness never fails
evidence: mutation run: 2 pytest failures, e2e FAIL on replay check

decision: ran pytest and e2e against a scratch Postgres 15 as well as SQLite
why: production uses Postgres and search takes a tsvector path there
result: 55 tests and 49 e2e checks green on both

decision: sent auth, cross-user access, the gate and CLI credentials to an independent opus reviewer
why: never count my own review as the verdict
